summary: Full backend (14/14 pytest passed) and frontend e2e tested for Work Orders app. Verified CRUD, sort_order DESC, reorder endpoint, Excel export with Spanish headers, attachment upload/download, search/filter. Frontend: create OT, edit OT, delete with confirm/cancel AlertDialog, Excel download trigger, filter panel open/apply/empty-state/clear, dashboard header + counter, 'Hoy' badge on today's OTs.

minor.issue: Endpoint sorts by created_at DESC instead of sort_order DESC (inconsistent with list endpoint after manual reorder). Excel rows will not reflect the user-defined order.
No file size limit / file type validation - any file accepted with arbitrary extension.

issues: Header looks clean with gradient logo and counter (shows 'X órdenes' correctly). Nothing critical.

action_items: (Optional) Consider sorting Excel export by sort_order DESC to match the UI order users see after manual drag-drop reordering.
(Optional) Add basic file validation (size/type) to upload endpoint.

Drag-and-drop UI was not exhaustively tested via Playwright (DnD is fragile to automate). The underlying /api/workorders/reorder endpoint is fully verified via pytest and persistence after reload was confirmed via API call from the browser context.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py export_to_excel uses sort by created_at instead of sort_order — inconsistent with main list ordering after manual reorder.
Dashboard.js is ~615 lines — could be split into smaller components (row, header, filters) to stay below 700 LOC threshold as feature grows.
handleClearFilters uses setTimeout(fetchWorkOrders, 100) which is brittle; better to call fetch directly with empty params or via useEffect on state change.

success_rate.frontend: 95% (all critical flows verified: create, edit, delete with AlertDialog, excel export download, filters open/apply/empty-state/clear, Hoy badge, counter)

seed_data_creation: Test fixtures auto-create and cleanup TEST_* and DD_TEST_* prefixed work orders. All cleaned up at end of test run.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend is rock solid - all CRUD, reorder, excel export, attachments, search/filter verified via pytest. Frontend works for all primary flows. The drag-and-drop UI interaction itself was not simulated via Playwright (use a real browser or react-beautiful-dnd test util if needed) but the /api/workorders/reorder endpoint and persistence-after-reload are confirmed. Minor consideration: excel export ignores sort_order (uses created_at) — may or may not be intentional.
